Hi @niviksha, thanks for the issue. It looks like Streamlit magics does not detect the output of `resolve_scale` as an Altair object, but you can display the Altair layer through `st.altair_chart` as a workaround.

Code sample : 

```python
import altair as alt
from altair.expr import datum
from vega_datasets import data
import streamlit as st

stocks = data.stocks.url

base = alt.Chart(stocks).encode(
    x='date:T',
    y='price:Q',
    color='symbol:N'
).transform_filter(
    datum.symbol == 'GOOG'
)

(base.mark_line() + base.mark_point()).resolve_scale(y='independent') # does not work
st.write((base.mark_line() + base.mark_point()).resolve_scale(y='independent')) # works
st.altair_chart((base.mark_line() + base.mark_point()).resolve_scale(y='independent')) # works
```

Running into this problem on 0.65 for any variation of the methods outlined above.

[![Open in Streamlit Cloud](https://static.streamlit.io/badges/streamlit_badge_black_white.svg)](https://issues.streamlitapp.com/?issue=gh-1667)

```

chart_test_failures = base.mark_line().encode(alt.Y('Test Failures:N'))

st.write((chart_test_count + chart_test_failures).resolve_scale(y='independent'))
st.altair_chart((chart_test_count + chart_test_failures).resolve_scale(y='independent'))

st.altair_chart(chart_test_count)
st.altair_chart(chart_test_failures)
st.altair_chart(chart_test_count | chart_test_failures)
```

issue.title: Concatenated altair plots rendered on top of each other when .resolve_scale() is in play

labels.name: priority:P2
labels.description: Medium-high priority - fix within one month

repository.name: streamlit
repository.description: Streamlit — A faster way to build and share data apps.

issue.body:
# Summary

Trying to show some vertically concatenated altair plots via `st.altair_chart()`, but the subplots are rendered on top of each other instead of proper vertical concatenation.

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12885402/82130176-4e885680-97c9-11ea-8245-6c42238be648.png)

Suspect is `.resolve_scale()` method, while customizing the legend via `legend=alt.Legend(title=None)` on each subplot or in `.configure_legend(title=None)` on the concatenated chart object _and_ keeping legend orient at right (either explicitly setting it or leaving out `orient` keyword).

It might be me misunderstanding how altair works, nevertheless the plots work just fine in a jupyter notebook. 

# Steps to reproduce

1. Create concatenated plot (with the `&` operator in my case)
2. Customize legend in either one of the following ways:
    1. add `legend=alt.Legend(title=None)` to the color channel on _all_ subplots
    2. add `.configure_legend(title=None)` to the concatenated chart object
3. Add `.resolve_scale(color="independent")` to the concatenated chart or any of the subplots
4.  Wrap the plot in `st.altair_chart()`

## Expected behavior:

I would expect Streamlit to properly show concatenated plots even when using `.resolve_scale()` and customized legends.

## Actual behavior:

I believe this code:

```python
# Dummy data
data1 = (
    pd.DataFrame(np.random.random(size=(30, 3)), columns=["A", "B", "C"])
    .reset_index()
    .melt(id_vars="index")
)
data2 = (
    pd.DataFrame(np.random.random(size=(30, 3)), columns=["D", "E", "F"])
    .reset_index()
    .melt(id_vars="index")
)

# Actual plot
st.altair_chart(
    (
        alt.Chart(data1).mark_area().encode(x="index", y="value", color="variable")
        & alt.Chart(data2).mark_area().encode(x="index", y="value", color="variable")
    )
    .configure_legend(title=None)
    .resolve_scale(color="independent")
)
```
results in this:

![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/12885402/82143508-c0ea4c80-9844-11ea-92df-a48669aa73c6.png)

__Notes:__

- This code works fine in jupyter notebook
- Removing `.configure_legend()` from the method chain fixes the rendering (but obviously leave legend title "variable" in place)
- Removing `title=None` fixes the rendering
- Setting `orient="right"` in `configure_legend()` results in the same plot
- Setting `orient="bottom"` in `configure_legend()` (while keeping `title=None`) fixes rendering (no legend title, plots appear one after the other)
- When I remove the `.resolve_scale()` method from the whole concatenated plot but keep it on one of the subplots (which is a layered plot itself), then only those subplots are "collapsed" that come _after_ the `.resolve_scale()` call in the concatenation order. Eg.:

```python
chart = (
    # First 3 plots rendered normally
    plot1
    & plot2
    & plot3
    # Subplots from here will be rendered over each other and plot1
    & (plot4 + plot5).resolve_scale(color="independent")
    & plot6
    & plot7
)
```

## Is this a regression?

I don't know.

# Debug info

- Streamlit version: 0.59.0 
- Python version: 3.7.4
- Using Conda? PipEnv? PyEnv? Pex?: virtualenv + pip
- OS version: macOS 10.14.6
- Browser version: Chrome 81.0.4044

### Summary

Altair chart won't show if use `resolve_scale`

### Steps to reproduce

Code snippet:

```python
import altair as alt
from vega_datasets import data
import streamlit as st


source = data.wheat()

bars = alt.Chart(source).mark_bar().encode(
    x='wheat:Q',
    y=alt.Y("year:O", sort="x")
)

text = bars.mark_text(
    align='left',
    dx=3  # Nudges text to right so it doesn't appear on top of the bar
).encode(
    text='wheat:Q',
)

c = (bars + text).resolve_scale(y='independent')

st.altair_chart(c)
```
No image shows, this is because streamlit add this to every altair chart

```
  "autosize": {
      "type": "fit",
      "contains": "padding"
  },
  "padding": {
      "bottom": 20
  }
```

which is conflict with 

```
    "resolve": {
        "scale": {
            "y": "independent"
        }
    },
```

issue.body:
### Checklist

- [X] I have searched the [existing issues](https://github.com/streamlit/streamlit/issues) for similar issues.
- [X] I added a very descriptive title to this issue.
- [X] I have provided sufficient information below to help reproduce this issue.

### Summary

Hello there,

When doing a compound plot in altair with interval interactions, the lines are not displayed properly. 
The images below will make it very clear.

Thanks a lot for your help ! 

### Reproducible Code Example

```python
# requirements.txt

streamlit==1.18.0
altair==4.2.2
pandas==1.3.3
altair_viewer==0.4.0
```

```python
# webapp.py

import streamlit as st
from altair_demo import main_altair

def main():
    st.write("Hello")
    chart = main_altair()
    st.altair_chart(altair_chart=chart)

if __name__ =="__main__":
    main()
```


```python
# altair_demo.py

import pandas as pd
import altair as alt

alt.renderers.enable('mimetype')

def main():
    data = pd._testing.makeTimeDataFrame(freq='H')
    data = data.reset_index().melt(id_vars="index")

    interval = alt.selection_interval(encodings=["x"])

    base = (
        alt.Chart(data=data)
        .mark_line(point={"filled": False, "fill": "white"}, strokeWidth=2)
        .encode(
            x=alt.X("index:T", title="Date"),
            y=alt.Y("value", title="Cible"),
        )
    )

    line_chart = (
        base.encode(
            x=alt.X("index:T", title="Date", scale=alt.Scale(domain=interval.ref())),
            color="variable",
        )
    ).properties(width=600, height=300)

    view = (
        base.add_selection(interval)
        .encode(color="variable")
        .properties(
            width=600,
            height=50,
        )
    )

    histogram = (
        alt.Chart(data=data)
        .mark_bar().encode(
            alt.X("value:Q", bin=True),
            y=alt.Y("count()"),
        )
    ).transform_filter(
        interval
    )

    return line_chart & view | histogram

if __name__ =="__main__":
    chart = main()
    # chart.show()
    st.altair_chart(chart)
```

### Steps To Reproduce
0. Create the files `requirements.txt`, `webapp.py` and `altair_demo.py`
1. `pip install -r requirements.txt`
2. `python altair_demo.py` -> Displaying chart at http://localhost:45747/
3. `streamlit run webapp.py` -> http://localhost:8501

### Expected Behavior

Pictures speak volume. 
Altair plot from the code below:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/78359781/218152458-b1f90ed5-0905-4ecc-a374-9e1df51b07b7.png)

### Current Behavior

Streamlit equivalent of the same plot:
![image](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/78359781/218152529-6bea20d7-14a4-46e3-984e-e47fc866da71.png)

### Is this a regression?

- [ ] Yes, this used to work in a previous version.

### Debug info

- Streamlit version: 1.18.0
- Python version: Python 3.8.10
- Operating System: Ubuntu 20.04 on Windows 11 WSL
- Browser: Firefox 109.0.1 (64-bit)
- Virtual environment: virtualenv 


### Additional Information

I think the issue was already raised here first: https://discuss.streamlit.io/t/data-missing-from-altair-compound-chart/11527

### Are you willing to submit a PR?

- [ ] Yes, I am willing to submit a PR!

## Describe your changes

This reverts commit f04178fe9690f4ff60551a2830dc59c7e84e9eb2.

The original intent was to layered discrete charts would always work (from issue #1667). However, upon analysis, we found people would prefer more a dynamic height based on the size of the step. Furthermore, setting the config is the workaround for #8642 and #1667. Upon inspection, we found people prefer supporting dynamic height first.

The better solution for #1667 is to suggest to the user to set the config discrete height for the resolve scale for clarity.

closes #8642

## Testing Plan

- This is a pure revert so tests should still pass.

---

body:
So we fixed the issue, but upon inspection, we broke another issue in #8642 . There does not seem to be a good solution to solve both. Based on the two problems, we are choosing to revert the change.

The workaround to address the issue here is to `.configure_view(discreteHeight=350, discreteHeight={"step": 20})` to get the chart to appear. Will monitor this issue, but I plan to keep it closed as expected behavior.
